mission: Gladstone AI advises the US government on national-security risks from advanced AI, especially weaponisation and loss of control. It trains officials (including hundreds of Defense Department staff) through its 'Foundations of AI' course, builds LLM test infrastructure for the Pentagon, and wrote the first US government-commissioned action plan on catastrophic AI risk.

key_work.title: Defense in Depth: An Action Plan to Increase the Safety and Security of Advanced AI
key_work.plain_summary: Commissioned by the US State Department and based on 200+ interviews, it warned advanced AI could pose an 'extinction-level threat' and proposed interim safeguards, early warning, a new regulator and international coordination.

key_work.title: America's Superintelligence Project
key_work.plain_summary: Argues that if the US builds superintelligence it must secure the whole chain (chips, data centres, labs) against Chinese espionage and sabotage, while not losing control of the system.

key_work.title: Foundations of AI course
key_work.plain_summary: A course training senior public- and private-sector leaders on AI capabilities, uses and risks.

warnings.text: Advanced AI creates new categories of weapons-of-mass-destruction-like risks.
Loss of control over advanced AI could pose an extinction-level threat to humanity.
Frontier labs' security is not good enough to stop theft or sabotage by states such as China.
A race between frontier labs, started by scaling after GPT-3, raises national-security risks.

recommendations.text: Adopt a 'defense in depth' plan: interim safeguards, early-warning systems and a new AI regulatory agency.
Consider licensing of large training runs above compute thresholds and limits on open-sourcing the most powerful weights (Action Plan).
Dramatically harden security around frontier AI projects.
Pursue international coordination and arms-control-style agreements on AI.
